bullets.title: Goldman: HFs selling tech/comms at 98th-pct intensity; hyperscalers outpacing semis
bullets.body: Goldman's floor desk flagged -5.5% better-for-sale overall, with hedge funds -15% better-for-sale in a 98th-pct reading over the past year—supply concentrated in Tech and Communications Services. Separately, Goldman noted a 'clear theme of buying Hyperscalers vs selling Semis,' with the Mag7 basket outperforming NDX by ~3% while the semiconductor/memory pair basket (GSPRHIMO) fell 6.5% on the day.

bullets.title: NVDA CEO Huang in Japan: denies Vera Rubin delay, confirms large-volume production
bullets.body: Jensen Huang, in Tokyo, stated 'the reports are not true' regarding AI server delays, saying Vera Rubin is already in production in 'giant amounts.' He also announced NVIDIA's partnership with Kawasaki Heavy Industries to build an AI-powered, robot-equipped shipyard, and met SEGA executives to celebrate the 1995 $5M investment that saved Nvidia from bankruptcy.

bullets.title: AMD Helios rack shipments reportedly delayed out of this year despite company denial
bullets.body: A source with claimed visibility into AMD's supply chain asserts Helios rack shipments are delayed beyond 2026, contradicting AMD's public denials. The source maintains confidence in their read despite the company's pushback.

bullets.title: SNDK and DELL suffer sharp intraday drops; memory fundamentals seen as strong despite selloff
bullets.body: SanDisk extended losses to a session-low of -11% while DELL dropped to a fresh session low of -8.5%, later extending to -13%—the worst performance since April 2025. One trader noted DRAM prices are expected to rise 20%+ next quarter with SNDK securing LTAs with META, calling the selloff a disconnect from fundamentals; separately, GFHK lowered Q3 DRAM price growth forecasts amid customer pushback but turned more positive on NAND.

bullets.title: AAPL hunting AI chip acquisitions; M2 Ultra fell short for AI workloads
bullets.body: Apple reportedly approached chip startups to gauge acquisition interest, per The Information, aiming to build proprietary server chips for AI. Separately, Apple's M2 Ultra chips were reported to have underperformed on advanced AI workloads, forcing reliance on Nvidia. AAPL also hit new all-time highs and is within $250B of the $5T market cap milestone.

bullets.title: Nokia and NVDA launch first AI-RAN platform; 20%+ spectral efficiency gains targeted
bullets.body: NOK and NVDA announced the first AI-RAN platform, delivering 20%+ spectral efficiency gains initially, targeting 50% by 2027 and 100%+ by 2028, sold as a software subscription rather than hardware. NOK is also trading near its prior earnings-day levels ahead of upcoming results, with one trader flagging it as an attractive entry despite Ericsson-related headwinds.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO as early as October at ~$1T implied valuation
bullets.body: Bloomberg reported Anthropic is targeting an IPO as early as October, planning investor meetings in coming weeks. The company raised $65B in a recent funding round at a $965B valuation, implying a $1T+ current value. Anthropic, Blackstone, and H&F also announced a separate AI services firm launch.

bullets.title: SPY 750 put wall cited as key support; $2B+ call wall building at 755
bullets.body: Options flow commentary noted SPY bears drove price down to the 750 put wall, described as 'the final line of support for bulls before a potential sharp decline.' The level held and produced a large intraday bounce; a $2B+ call wall is now building at 755.

bullets.title: Fed's Cook signals hold in July, prepared to act in September if inflation doesn't slow
bullets.body: Fed Governor Lisa Cook stated it is prudent to wait 'a bit more time' for inflation to slow, but said she is 'prepared to act' if disinflation signals don't emerge soon. Cook attributed the FOMC's hawkish evolution to AI buildout spending showing no signs of slowdown, and noted risk assessment has shifted toward higher inflation concerns since last summer.

bullets.title: PPI June -0.3% MoM, well below 0.0% estimate; YoY at 5.5% vs 6.2% expected
bullets.body: June PPI fell 0.3% month-over-month (vs. 0.0% consensus) and rose 5.5% year-over-year (vs. 6.2% estimate), with core PPI at 4.7% vs. 5.1% expected. Nearly two-thirds of the goods decline was driven by a 12% gasoline price drop. Multiple sources noted this effectively takes a July rate hike off the table.

bullets.title: Empire State Manufacturing surges to +15.6 in July vs +9.2 est; broad-based strength
bullets.body: The July NY Empire State Manufacturing Index printed +15.6, well above the +9.2 consensus and prior +5.7, with new orders moving sharply higher, prices paid easing, and employment strengthening. The beat was characterized as broad-based.

bullets.title: Uber nearing €12.5B deal to acquire Delivery Hero; announcement expected Thursday
bullets.body: Uber is reported to be in advanced negotiations to acquire Delivery Hero for approximately €12.5 billion, with an announcement potentially as early as Thursday. As part of the deal, Delivery Hero would divest its Turkish unit Yemeksepeti and several European businesses to an investment firm.

bullets.title: GOOGL: pulls out of Epic ruling appeal; to permit third-party app stores next week
bullets.body: Google withdrew its request to change the court ruling in the Epic antitrust case, avoiding further litigation. Separately, Google announced it will permit third-party stores in its app store starting next week, marking a regulatory shift in app distribution.

bullets.title: META OTM call sweep: $12M notional, 2-month expiry
bullets.body: A flow-monitoring account flagged $12M in out-of-the-money META call options with a two-month expiry, suggesting speculative or directional positioning in the name. META's market cap has also surpassed Saudi Aramco's, and is now 28% larger than MSFT.

bullets.title: NVDA put sweepers detected; semis ETF SMH down 3.7% intraday
bullets.body: Large NVDA put sweepers were detected, signaling downside hedging or directional bearish flow. The $SMH semiconductor ETF fell 3.7% from the open despite an initially higher open, with one analyst noting semis have not been down more than 2% on a day the Nasdaq finished higher since November 2024.

bullets.title: BABA jumps 5.7% on report Alibaba's Qwen AI to be integrated into Apple Intelligence in China
bullets.body: U.S.-listed Alibaba shares rallied 5.7% on reports that its Qwen AI model will be integrated into Apple Intelligence for the China market, directly benefiting from Apple's AI localization strategy.

bullets.title: Iran-US escalation: Hormuz, naval blockade, and US strikes continue
bullets.body: US forces restarted a naval blockade of Iranian ports, redirecting two commercial vessels, while Trump signaled strikes against Iran would expand next week per Fox News. Iran's top negotiator Qalibaf stated Iran's national security hinges on maintaining control of the Strait of Hormuz and framed negotiations as part of a resistance strategy rather than compromise.

bullets.title: Trump bullish on data centers; files up to $1M EQIX purchase; NY moratorium controversy
bullets.body: Trump stated data centers are 'one of the biggest driving forces for future jobs' and filed a purchase order for up to $1M of EQIX stock. He criticized NY Governor Hochul for terminating data center projects for 'political reasons,' prompting bipartisan criticism. China was noted as imposing no data center moratoriums, framing the US regulatory friction as an AI competitiveness risk.

bullets.title: Warsh: Fed missed inflation target for 63 months; AI may or may not be inflationary
bullets.body: Kevin Warsh testified that the Fed has missed its inflation target for 63 months and signaled he wants to review the balance sheet and rate-setting methods. He stated whether AI is inflationary or deflationary will be up to Fed policy decisions, and distanced himself from characterizing AI infrastructure spending as inherently inflationary—a divergence from some FOMC colleagues.

bullets.title: IPO volume hits highest level since 2021; Morgan Stanley wealth drew $148B in Q2, 50%+ from IPOs
bullets.body: IPO market activity reached its highest level since 2021 driven by AI-focused deals. Morgan Stanley's wealth management division attracted $148B of new assets in Q2, with more than half linked to new IPOs, signaling that the IPO pipeline is converting meaningfully into client flows.
